metadata.headline: Is Rebag really a marketplace if it buys the inventory itself?

platform_lesson.title: A digital intermediary is not automatically a marketplace
platform_lesson.text: Rebag connects people who want to sell luxury goods with people who want to buy them, but the transaction architecture is not the same as a peer-to-peer marketplace. Sellers commonly transfer the item into Rebag's controlled buyout or consignment process; Rebag authenticates, prices and lists it, and the Buyer purchases from Rebag's curated inventory. The PBMC therefore shows two exchanges through the Owner rather than one direct Provider-to-Consumer transaction. The platform lesson is that having two participant groups does not by itself make a business a marketplace.

core_value_unit.explanation: The Authenticated Item is the Core Value Unit: a luxury handbag, accessory, watch or jewelry item that Rebag has accepted, vetted and made available for resale.

metrics.note: Rebag states that shoppers can browse thousands of one-of-a-kind items from more than 50 designer brands.

actor.explanation: Shoppers seeking authenticated pre-owned luxury handbags, accessories, watches and jewelry.

job.explanation: Buyers want desirable luxury products with lower authenticity risk than an unverified resale transaction.

gain.explanation: Rebag combines curated inventory, authentication, resale-price information and physical/digital shopping channels.

pain.explanation: Luxury Buyers face counterfeit risk, condition uncertainty, high prices and uncertain resale value.

transaction.explanation: The Buyer pays Rebag for an item from Rebag's curated inventory.

filter.explanation: Purchase depends on payment, geographic availability and the one-of-a-kind nature of resale inventory.

access_channel.explanation: Buyers shop through Rebag.com, the mobile app and physical Rebag locations.

activities.explanation: Buyers search, compare, buy, finance, trade or use Rebag's resale-value tools.

resources.explanation: Buyers contribute purchasing power, style preferences and demand signals.

actor.explanation: Individuals provide pre-owned luxury items to Rebag through buyout, consignment or trade processes.

job.explanation: Sellers want to turn high-value luxury items into cash, credit or consignment proceeds with less transaction friction.

gain.explanation: Clair can provide rapid pricing guidance or offers, while stores and mail-in flows reduce the effort of finding an end Buyer.

pain.explanation: Sellers may disagree with Rebag's quote, wait for consignment sale or have items rejected after inspection.

transaction.explanation: The Seller gives the item to Rebag and receives an offer, eventual consignment payout or trade value depending on the route.

filter.explanation: Rebag only accepts selected designers and vets condition and authenticity before an item enters inventory.

access_channel.explanation: Sellers can use Clair online, submit images, ship items or visit a Rebag store.

activities.explanation: Sellers identify the item, request a quote, submit or consign it and accept the resulting commercial terms.

resources.explanation: The key Provider resource is the authentic pre-owned luxury item plus accurate information about model and condition.

actor.explanation: Payments, logistics, financing and retail-property services support Rebag's resale operation.

job.explanation: Service Partners help Rebag move money, goods and customers across online and physical channels.

gain.explanation: High-value resale creates payment, shipping, financing and retail-service demand.

pain.explanation: Luxury goods create high exposure to fraud, chargebacks, loss, damage and service errors.

transaction.explanation: Partners provide enabling services to Rebag in return for commercial compensation.

filter.explanation: Partners need reliability, security and service quality appropriate to high-value goods.

access_channel.explanation: Partners connect through payment, logistics, retail and technical integrations.

activities.explanation: Partners process payments, ship, finance, insure or support physical retail.

resources.explanation: Partners contribute transaction rails, delivery networks, real estate or operational infrastructure.

actor.explanation: Rebag is the central buyer, curator, authenticator and reseller in the transaction. Unlike a classic peer-to-peer marketplace, it often takes the item into its own controlled inventory flow before selling it onward.

job.explanation: Rebag turns heterogeneous luxury supply into a standardized, trusted resale assortment.

gain.explanation: By controlling pricing, authentication and the customer experience, Rebag can earn resale margin and build a premium trust brand.

pain.explanation: Taking control of goods creates inventory, authentication, pricing, return and working-capital risk that a lighter marketplace can push to participants.

transaction.explanation: Rebag buys, consigns or accepts luxury items from Sellers and then resells authenticated inventory to Buyers.

governance.explanation: Rebag controls accepted brands, condition standards, authentication, pricing logic and item eligibility.

promotion_channel.explanation: Rebag attracts demand through digital marketing, Clair reports, its app, luxury content and physical retail.

activities.explanation: Rebag prices, vets, authenticates, photographs, lists, stores and sells items.

resources.explanation: Clair pricing data, authentication expertise, luxury inventory, physical stores and operating know-how are central resources.

current.explanation: Luxury Buyers pay Rebag for authenticated inventory.
Rebag provides the vetted luxury item to the Buyer.
Luxury Sellers send or bring items to Rebag for buyout, consignment or trade.
Rebag provides a quote and pays or credits the Seller according to the selected resale route.
Commerce partners provide payment, logistics, financing or retail support.
Rebag creates transaction and service volume for supporting partners.

metrics.note: Rebag sells thousands of one-of-a-kind items across 50+ designer brands.
